simple.meaning: עַמּוֹנִית (ʻAmmôwnîyth) is a Hebrew word meaning “an Ammonitess.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: עַמּוֹנִית (H5985) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Kings 14:21, with occurrences in 1 Kings, 2 Chronicles.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עַמּוֹנִית (H5985) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in עַמּוֹנִית (H5985) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: עַמּוֹנִית (ʻAmmôwnîyth) / H5985 is traced through 1 Kings 14:21, 1 Kings 14:31, 2 Chronicles 12:13, 2 Chronicles 24:26 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which Yahweh had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonitess.

timeline.evidenceText: Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigned in Judah. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which Yahweh had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonitess.
Rehoboam slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in David’s city. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonitess. Abijam his son reigned in his place.

So king Rehoboam strengthened himself in Jerusalem and reigned; for Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which Yahweh had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. His mother’s name was Naamah the Ammonitess.
These are those who conspired against him: Zabad the son of Shimeath the Ammonitess and Jehozabad the son of Shimrith the Moabitess.
